mainTopic: Enactments from אושא (supporting children, the one-fifth limit on צדקה, training a son, a wife's נכסי מלוג), the right ages for learning, and פסוקים about צדקה and grandchildren.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about רבי יונתן, who had to force some sons to feed their father. The גמרא uses it to show that an earlier אושא ordinance was not enforced as strict law. Next comes another אושא ordinance: do not give more than a fifth of your money to צדקה, so you do not end up needing help yourself. A ברייתא and a story support it, and the גמרא finds a hint in יעקב's double tithe. רב יצחק then reports that a father should be gentle with his son until twelve. The גמרא reconciles this with רב's advice to push children hard from age six, using the ages אביי's mother taught for מקרא and משנה. It also brings her advice about dangerous stings, and רב קטינא's two-sided warning about starting school before six. After one more אושא ruling, about a wife's נכסי מלוג, the גמרא explains several פסוקים from תהלים about constant צדקה and the blessing of grandchildren. It ends by returning to the משנה's teaching of רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Why would רבי יונתן need to force the sons?
steps.stepSummary: The story ends with רבי יונתן forcing the sons to feed their father. The גמרא argues that this only makes sense if feeding him was not the actual law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I forced them, and they fed him. Now, if you say it was not the law, that is why he had to force them. But if you say it was the law, why would he need to force them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a story about רבי יונתן. It then uses the story to attack the idea that the earlier אושא ordinance is binding law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sons were legally required to feed their father, the court could simply have taken the money from the property. The fact that רבי יונתן had to push the sons to do it themselves suggests there was no legal obligation. So the ordinance was not accepted as law.

keyTerms.meaning: I forced them / I pressured them
It makes sense / granted (the first side of a 'this works, but that doesn't' argument)
The law; what the court can actually enforce

steps.whatToRemember: Because רבי יונתן had to force the sons, the גמרא concludes that the ordinance about feeding a father from property he gave his sons was not enforced as strict law.
steps.confusionAlert: The question 'did he need to force them?' is not asking for information. It is a challenge: if it were the law, forcing them would be unnecessary.

phrases.english: And I forced them, and they fed him.
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'to feed him' (round brackets); the corrected wording, in square brackets, says 'and they fed him.'

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is not the law,
that is why he had to force them.
But if you say it is the law,
would he need to force them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אי אמרת בשלמא לאו דינא משום הכי עשיינהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story quoted before this section and uses it as a challenge to the earlier אושא ordinance.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the אושא ordinance about feeding a father from property he gave his sons is binding law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forcing the sons is only necessary if the law did not already require it. So the story shows it was not the law.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ordinance was not accepted as enforceable law.

steps.title: Do not give away more than a fifth
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא reports another ordinance made in אושא: someone giving away money to צדקה should not give more than one-fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: In אושא they made an ordinance that one who gives away his money generously should not give away more than a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, another ordinance from אושא. It sets a maximum on how much a person should give to צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving צדקה is a great מצוה, but the חכמים set an upper limit of one-fifth. This is a new rule and is not connected to the previous discussion about feeding a father, except that it also comes from אושא.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in the גליל where the חכמים met and made important ordinances
One who gives away / spends generously (here, on צדקה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known הלכה that a person generally should not give more than a fifth of his money to צדקה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said:
In Usha they made an ordinance:
One who gives away his money should not give away more than a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אילעא באושא התקינו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a different ordinance from אושא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should not give away more than one-fifth of his money to צדקה.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same rule and gives the reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same one-fifth limit and explains why: so the giver does not end up needing help from others.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: One who gives away his money should not give away more than a fifth, in case he will come to need other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי אילעא's ordinance. The ברייתא also adds the reason for the limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new information here is the reason. If someone gives away too much, he may become poor and need צדקה from others himself. The limit protects the giver.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports what was just said)
He will need other people (to support him)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who gives away his money should not give away more than a fifth,
in case he will come to need other people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא נמי הכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אילעא's ordinance with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The one-fifth limit on giving צדקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording, which also gives the reason.

steps.title: A story: a friend stops someone from giving too much
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells a story about someone who wanted to give more than a fifth, and his friend would not let him. There are two versions of who was who.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story about someone who wanted to give away more than a fifth, and his friend did not let him. Who was the friend? רבי ישבב. Some say רבי ישבב was the one giving, and his friend did not let him. And who was the friend? רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a real story showing the one-fifth rule being kept. Then it gives two opinions about which חכמים were in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that even great חכמים held back a friend from giving too much. In the first version, רבי ישבב stopped someone. In the second version, רבי ישבב wanted to give and רבי עקיבא stopped him.

keyTerms.meaning: A story / an event that happened

phrases.english: And there was a story about one who wanted to give away more than a fifth,
and his friend did not let him.
And who was the friend? Rabbi Yeshevav.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב, וְלֹא הִנִּיחוֹ חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: And some say: it was Rabbi Yeshevav who wanted to give, and his friend did not let him,
and who was the friend? Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: ומעשה באחד שבקש לבזבז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a story that shows the rule being kept.
steps.raayaObject: The one-fifth limit was kept in practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about רבי ישבב and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The פסוק hint: יעקב's double tithe
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן (or רב אחא בר יעקב) finds a hint for the one-fifth limit in יעקב's promise, where the word for 'tithe' appears twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said, and some say it was רב אחא בר יעקב: What is the פסוק that hints to this? 'And all that You give me, I will surely tithe it for You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks for a source in the תורה for the one-fifth limit. It points to יעקב's promise in בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'עשר אעשרנו' uses the word 'tithe' twice. That suggests two tenths, and two tenths make one-fifth. So יעקב promised to give a fifth, which is understood as the maximum.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (that teaches this)?
And some say (it was a different אמורא)
I will surely tithe it (literally 'tithe, I will tithe it')

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said, and some say it was Rav Acha bar Ya'akov:
What is the verse?
"And all that You give me,
I will surely tithe it for You."
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:22. The word 'tithe' is said twice, which means two tenths, which is a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי קרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק that hints to the one-fifth limit from step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 28:22, with the doubled word 'עשר אעשרנו'.

steps.title: The second tenth is smaller than the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that two tithes taken one after the other do not equal a fifth, because the second is a tenth of what is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the second tenth is not like the first tenth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from the פסוק in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you take a tenth and then a tenth of what remains, the second tenth is smaller. For example, from 100 you give 10, then a tenth of 90, which is 9. Together that is 19, not 20, so it is not quite a fifth.

phrases.english: But the second tenth is not similar
to the first tenth!
phrases.notes: The second tenth is taken from a smaller amount, so the total comes out a little less than a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: והא לא דמי עישורא בתרא לעישורא קמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'עשר אעשרנו' adds up to one-fifth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two tithes taken one after another add up to less than a fifth, since the second comes from what is left over.

steps.title: רב אשי: the second tenth equals the first
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the word 'אעשרנו' ('I will tithe IT') teaches that the second tenth is the same size as the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'אעשרנו' ('I will tithe it') means the second tenth is like the first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge from step 6 and saves the proof from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra ending '-נו' ('it') points back to the original whole amount. So both tenths are measured from the full amount, and together they make exactly one-fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: I will tithe it (the '-נו' means 'it', pointing to the original amount)

steps.whatToRemember: The upper limit for צדקה is one-fifth. It comes from יעקב's double tithe, where both tenths are measured from the original amount, so together they make a full fifth.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
"I will tithe it" means the second tenth is like the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אשי אעשרנו לבתרא כי קמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of the exact wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two tithes taken one after another would add up to less than a fifth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'אעשרנו' shows that both tenths are measured from the original amount, so together they make exactly one-fifth.

steps.title: The chain of names gets shorter, plus a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי notes that the אושא teachings come with fewer and fewer names behind them, and gives a memory aid for their order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: These teachings keep getting smaller. Your memory aid is: little ones, wrote, spent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the group of אושא teachings it just learned. It adds a comment about how they were passed down and gives a memory aid for their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is taught here. The comment is about how the teachings were reported: each one in the series is quoted with a shorter chain of names than the one before. The three words of the memory aid each point to one of the three teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: Teachings that were heard and passed down
Spent freely, gave away a lot (here, to צדקה)

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the three אושא teachings that רבי אילעא reported: supporting young children, writing property over to sons, and the one-fifth limit on giving צדקה.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
And these teachings keep getting smaller.
phrases.notes: He means the list of rabbis quoted behind each אושא teaching gets shorter each time.

phrases.english: And your memory aid: little ones, wrote, spent.
phrases.notes: Each word points to one teaching: supporting little children, writing property over to sons, and giving a lot to צדקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּעוֹת הַלָּלוּ מִתְמַעֲטוֹת וְהוֹלְכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the three אושא teachings reported by רבי אילעא, of which the one-fifth limit was the last. More אושא enactments follow in steps 9 and 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אושא teachings are quoted with fewer and fewer names, and are remembered by the words קטנים, כתבו, בזבזו.

steps.title: Be gentle with a son until twelve, then you may be strict
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק reports another אושא enactment: a father should be patient with his son until age twelve, and after that he may press him hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק said: In אושא they decided that a man should be gentle with his son until twelve years old. From then on, he may come down hard on him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אושא enactment is taught, about raising and teaching a son. It sets twelve as the age when a father may start being strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until twelve, the father should go easy even if the son does not want to learn. After twelve, he is allowed to put real pressure on him to learn.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the חכמים made these enactments
They enacted, they made a rule
Goes along gently with his son
Comes down hard on him, presses him strongly

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak said,
In Usha they enacted
that a person should go along gently with his son,
until twelve years old.
From here on,
he comes down hard on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק, בְּאוּשָׁא הִתְקִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אושא enactment on a new topic: training a son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father is gentle with his son until twelve, and after that may be strict with him.

steps.title: But רב said to push a six-year-old hard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יצחק from רב's instruction to a teacher: accept children at six and stuff them with learning like an ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב told רב שמואל בר שילת: under six, do not accept him. At six, accept him and stuff him like an ox!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'gentle until twelve' rule. רב told a teacher to push children hard from age six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק says no strong pressure until twelve. רב says to load a child up with learning from six. These seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Stuff him like an ox, feed him a lot

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav say
to Rav Shmuel bar Shilat:
Less than six years old, do not accept him.
Six years old, accept him
and stuff him like an ox!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יצחק's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק's rule that a father should be gentle until twelve
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב demands strong pressure on learning from age six, which seems to contradict being gentle until twelve.

steps.title: Teach hard from six, but harsh pressure only after twelve
steps.stepSummary: First answer: yes, you teach him intensively from six, but you do not come down hard on him until after twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, you stuff him like an ox. But you do not come down hard on him until after twelve years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both statements are true because they talk about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching a lot is one thing; harshly pushing a child who refuses is another. From six you teach him a great deal, but if he refuses, you may only press him hard after twelve.

phrases.english: Yes, he stuffs him like an ox,
however, he does not come down hard on him
until after twelve years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, סָפֵי לֵיהּ כְּתוֹרָא, מִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'stuff him like an ox' and 'gentle until twelve' describe the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Heavy teaching starts at six; harsh pressure on a child who refuses waits until after twelve.

steps.title: Six is for מקרא, the later age is for משנה
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: רב's age of six is for learning מקרא, and the later age is for learning משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say it is no problem: this one is for מקרא, that one is for משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer. The two statements talk about two different subjects of learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the difference is not the kind of pressure but what is being learned. Pushing from six is for מקרא (תנ"ך); the later age, in רב יצחק's rule, is for משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (a second answer)

phrases.english: And if you want, say it is not a problem:
this one is for Bible,
phrases.notes: "This one" is רב's age of six.

phrases.english: that one is for Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא לְמִקְרָא, הָא לְמִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two statements by subject of learning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements are about the same kind of learning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Six is the age to push for מקרא; the later age is for משנה.

steps.title: אביי's mother gives the right ages
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports what his mother told him: six for מקרא, ten for משנה, thirteen for a full-day fast, and twelve for a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אביי said: My mother told me: at six, for מקרא; at ten, for משנה; at thirteen, for fasting a full day. And a girl, at twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second answer. אביי's mother gave different ages for starting מקרא and starting משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that מקרא and משנה really do start at different ages, so the two statements can be about different subjects. She also adds the age for fasting a full day: thirteen for a boy, twelve for a girl.
steps.whatToRemember: Ages: six for מקרא, ten for משנה, thirteen for a boy to fast a full day, twelve for a girl.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. The first splits by kind of pressure; the second splits by subject, and only the second is backed by אביי.

phrases.english: As Abaye said: My mother told me:
A six-year-old, for Bible,
a ten-year-old, for Mishnah,
a thirteen-year-old, for fasting a full day.
And for a girl, twelve years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אֲמַרָה לִי אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second answer by showing מקרא and משנה start at different ages.
steps.raayaObject: The second answer, that the ages differ for מקרא and משנה

steps.title: אביי's mother: dangerous stings on a child's birthday and their cures
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports his mother's advice: a six-year-old stung by a scorpion on his sixth birthday, or a one-year-old stung by a hornet on his first birthday, is in mortal danger. She also gives the cure for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: A six-year-old who is stung by a scorpion on the day he turns six will not live. What is his cure? The bile of a white vulture in beer. Rub him with it and give him some to drink. A one-year-old who is stung by a hornet on the day he turns one will not live. What is his cure? Palm-tree fiber in water. Rub him with it and give him some to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last step quoted אביי's mother, the גמרא brings another piece of advice from her, this time about medical dangers to young children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are built the same way: a child stung on the exact day he completes a certain age, followed by a cure. Both cures are rubbed on the child and also given to him to drink. The link to the earlier steps is the topic of children's ages and the source, אביי's mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Rub him with it and make him drink it

phrases.english: Abaye said: My mother told me:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי בַּר שֵׁית דְּטָרְקָא לֵיהּ עַקְרַבָּא
phrases.english: A six-year-old who is stung by a scorpion
on the day he completes six years will not live.
What is his cure?
The bile of a white vulture in beer.
One should rub him with it and make him drink it.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי בַּר שַׁתָּא דְּטָרֵיק לֵיהּ זִיבּוּרָא
phrases.english: A one-year-old who is stung by a hornet
on the day he completes one year will not live.
What is his cure?
Palm-tree fiber in water.
One should rub him with it and make him drink it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אֲמַרָה לִי אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching from the same source as step 13 (אביי's mother), moving from the ages for learning to medical dangers at certain ages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child stung on the exact day he turns six (scorpion) or one (hornet) is in mortal danger. The cures are vulture bile in beer, or palm fiber in water, rubbed on and drunk.

steps.title: רב קטינא: starting school before age six
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא says that whoever brings his son to school before age six will run after him and not catch him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: Anyone who brings his son to school when he is younger than six will run after him and not catch him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of the right age to start school and brings רב קטינא's warning about starting too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to רב's instruction (step 10) to accept children at six. רב קטינא's phrase 'run after him and not catch him' is unclear: it can mean the father will keep worrying about a weakened child. The next steps show that it can also be read in a positive way.

keyTerms.meaning: One who brings his son in (to school)
Runs after him and does not catch him

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said:
Anyone who brings his son in
phrases.notes: The גמרא means bringing him into school to start learning.

phrases.english: when he is younger than six
will run after him and not catch him.
phrases.notes: In this version it's a warning: the father will keep worrying about a child weakened by too much learning too young.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the topic of steps 10-13 (six as the age to start learning) and warns against starting before six.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bringing a child to school before age six leads to trouble: the father will 'run after him and not catch him.'

steps.title: Another version: his friends cannot catch up with him
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב קטינא's words the opposite way: the child's friends will run after him and not catch up with him, because he will be far ahead in learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: His friends will run after him and not catch up with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב קטינא's statement, and this version praises an early start instead of warning against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the father is the one who 'runs after' a weak child. Here the friends are the ones who 'run after' him, because the early starter is so far ahead that they never catch up. So now the two versions seem to say opposite things.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (another version of the statement)

phrases.english: There are those who say:
His friends run after him
and do not catch up with him.
phrases.notes: He started early, so he is far ahead of them in learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב קטינא's words, which praises what the first version warned against.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Starting before six makes the child so successful that his friends cannot catch up with him.

steps.title: Both versions are true: he gets weaker but learns well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two versions do not argue: an early starter becomes physically weaker but also learns very well.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are true: he becomes weak, and he learns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash between the two versions of רב קטינא by saying that both results happen to the same child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of choosing one version, the גמרא says each one describes a different side of the same child. His body pays a price (the father worries), while his learning gains (friends can't catch up).

keyTerms.meaning: He becomes weak and he learns

phrases.english: And both are true:
he weakens and he learns.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ אִיתַנְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent contradiction between the two versions in steps 15 and 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both statements are true at once, each describing a different effect on the same child.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two versions seem to argue about whether an early start is harmful or helpful.
steps.terutzMaskana: An early start harms the child's health and helps his learning, so both versions are correct.

steps.title: Or: it depends on whether the child is weak or healthy
steps.stepSummary: A second way to reconcile the versions: the warning is about a weak child, and the praise is about a healthy child.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: This version is about a weak child, and that version is about a healthy child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to reconcile the two versions: they are talking about two different kinds of children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first answer, the same child gets both results. Here each version is about a different child: a weak child should not start early, and the father will worry about him. A healthy child can start early and will be far ahead of his friends.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: רב קטינא's warning about starting school before six is read two ways. Either an early start weakens the body but strengthens the learning, or it depends on whether the child is weak or healthy.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
This is about a weak child, that is about a healthy child.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same contradiction that step 17 resolved.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: each version is about a different type of child.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both versions seem to be about the same child and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The warning is for a weak child and the praise is for a healthy child.

steps.title: אושא enactment: the husband can take back the wife's sold נכסי מלוג
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא reports that in אושא they enacted: if a wife sold her נכסי מלוג while her husband was alive and then she died, the husband can take the property back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: In אושא they enacted: A woman who sold her נכסי מלוג while her husband was alive, and then she died, the husband can take it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of enactments made in אושא (like the one in step 9) and brings a new one about a wife's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נכסי מלוג belong to the wife, but the husband eats the produce while they are married, and he inherits her if she dies. The enactment says her sale during the marriage does not hold against him once she dies, so the property goes back to the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the חכמים made several enactments
The wife's property; she owns it, but the husband eats its produce

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
In Usha they enacted:
A woman who sold her usufruct property
phrases.notes: This is property she owns while her husband gets to eat what it produces.

phrases.english: during her husband's lifetime, and then she died,
the husband takes it back from the buyers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא, בְּאוּשָׁא הִתְקִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of school ages and returns to the series of אושא enactments, adding one about property.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a wife's sale of her נכסי מלוג is not final against her husband: if she dies first, the property goes back to him as her heir.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a wife sells her נכסי מלוג during the marriage and then dies, the husband may take the property back from the buyers.

steps.title: רב יצחק בר יוסף asks who taught the אושא rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף finds רבי אבהו standing in the crowd of אושא and asks him who is the source of the אושא rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף found רבי אבהו standing in the crowd of אושא. He said to him: Who is the master of the teaching of אושא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about the enactment from the last step. Here רב יצחק בר יוסף asks a question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about who reported the teaching, not about the law itself. רב יצחק בר יוסף wants to know which חכם the אושא rule should be quoted in the name of.

keyTerms.meaning: A crowd, a gathering of people

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef found Rabbi Abbahu
who was standing in the crowd of Usha.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן מָרַהּ דִּשְׁמַעְתָּא דְאוּשָׁא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Who is the master of the teaching of Usha?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story about how the אושא rule of step 19 was passed on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which חכם is the source of the אושא rule about נכסי מלוג.

steps.title: The answer: רבי יוסי בר חנינא; learned forty times
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the source is רבי יוסי בר חנינא. רב יצחק בר יוסף then learns it from him forty times, until it feels like it is sitting in his pocket.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יוסי בר חנינא. He learned it from him forty times, and it seemed to him as if it were placed in his pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question, and the story ends by telling how carefully רב יצחק בר יוסף reviewed the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer confirms the name given in step 19: רבי יוסי בר חנינא. Reviewing it forty times made the teaching his own, as safe and easy to reach as something in his pocket.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina.
He learned it from him forty times,
phrases.notes: רב יצחק בר יוסף reviewed it with רבי אבהו forty times.

phrases.aramaic: וְדָמֵי לֵיהּ כְּמַאן דְּמַנְּחָא לֵיהּ בְּכִיסְתֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: and it seemed to him as if it were placed in his pocket.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 20 and closes the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teaching is from רבי יוסי בר חנינא. רב יצחק בר יוסף reviewed it forty times until he knew it perfectly.

steps.title: How can anyone do צדקה at all times?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'Happy are those who keep justice, who do צדקה at all times' and asks: is it really possible to give צדקה at every moment?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Happy are those who keep justice, who do צדקה at all times.' But is it possible to do צדקה at all times?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק and points out a difficulty in its plain meaning. This sets up the explanations in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can't be giving צדקה every single moment, since a poor person isn't always in front of you. So the גמרא looks for a kind of צדקה that really does go on all the time.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it possible? (a question on the plain meaning)

phrases.english: "Happy are those who keep justice,
who do charity at all times."

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹת צְדָקָה בְּכׇל עֵת?
phrases.english: But is it possible to do charity at all times?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹת צְדָקָה בְּכׇל עֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a פסוק about constant צדקה, which ties back to the daf's theme of supporting young children.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of צדקה can a person really be doing 'at all times'?

steps.title: Feeding your young children is constant צדקה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of יבנה, or רבי אליעזר, explain that the פסוק refers to someone who feeds his sons and daughters while they are young.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Rabbis in יבנה explained, and some say it was רבי אליעזר: This is someone who feeds his sons and daughters when they are young.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer to the question: a father supporting his young children is doing צדקה all the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding one's children never stops; it goes on every day, so it fits 'at all times.' Calling it צדקה connects to the daf's theme of supporting young children: the father is praised as doing charity when he feeds them.

phrases.english: Our Rabbis in Yavne explained,
and some say it was Rabbi Eliezer:
This is one who feeds his sons and daughters
when they are young.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁבְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Constant צדקה means feeding one's own young sons and daughters, which goes on every day.

steps.title: Raising orphans at home is constant צדקה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives another explanation: the פסוק refers to someone who raises an orphan boy or girl in his home and marries them off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: This is someone who raises an orphan boy or an orphan girl in his home and marries them off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the same question: taking orphans into your home is the constant צדקה of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first answer, this is a kindness that goes on every day. But here the children are not one's own: the person raises orphans in his house and continues until he marries them off.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphan boy and an orphan girl

steps.whatToRemember: 'Doing צדקה at all times' means a kindness that never stops: either feeding your own young children, or raising orphans in your home until you marry them off.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
This is one who raises an orphan boy or an orphan girl
in his home and marries them off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 22, different from the answer in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Constant צדקה means raising orphans in one's home and marrying them off.

steps.title: A verse that seems to say two opposite things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק that says a person's wealth stays in his house while his צדקה lasts forever, which raises a hidden question.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Wealth and riches are in his house, and his צדקה stands forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק from תהלים. This sets up the next move, where two אמוראים explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not spoken out loud, but it is built into the פסוק. If someone gives his money away as צדקה, how can the money still be in his house? The next steps answer this puzzle.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands forever, lasts for all time

steps.confusionAlert: There is no question word here. The גמרא simply quotes the פסוק and expects you to notice the problem: giving money away and keeping it seem to clash.

phrases.english: 'Wealth and riches are in his house,
and his charity stands forever.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹן וָעוֹשֶׁר בְּבֵיתוֹ וְצִדְקָתוֹ עוֹמֶדֶת לָעַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of פסוקים about צדקה that began in step 22 with a new, similar פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a person keep his wealth at home and still have his צדקה last forever?

steps.title: First answer: one who learns תורה and teaches it
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא argue. One says the פסוק is about someone who learns תורה and teaches it to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One says: this is a person who learns תורה and teaches it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different explanations of the פסוק. Here is the first one: a person who learns תורה and teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you teach תורה, you lose none of your own knowledge. The 'wealth' (your תורה) stays with you, but the kindness you did for your students lasts forever.

keyTerms.meaning: One of them said (we are not told which one)
One who learns תורה and teaches it

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: זֶה הַלּוֹמֵד תּוֹרָה וּמְלַמְּדָהּ.
phrases.english: One said: This is one who learns Torah and teaches it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to someone who learns תורה and teaches it; he keeps his knowledge while others gain from it forever.

steps.title: Second answer: one who writes holy books and lends them
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says the פסוק is about someone who writes תורה, נביאים and כתובים and lends them to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one says: this is a person who writes תורה, נביאים and כתובים and lends them to others.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second explanation of the same פסוק. The person writes holy books and lends them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The books stay his, so the 'wealth' stays in his house. But other people learn from them, so his צדקה keeps going forever. This answer is about something physical you own, while the first answer was about knowledge.

keyTerms.meaning: The three parts of תנ״ך: תורה, נביאים, כתובים

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers solve the puzzle the same way: you give to others something you never lose. One says teaching תורה; the other says lending holy books.

phrases.english: And one said: This is one who writes
Torah, Prophets and Writings
and lends them to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: זֶה הַכּוֹתֵב תּוֹרָה נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to someone who writes holy books and lends them; the books stay his while others benefit forever.

steps.title: Grandchildren bring peace: no need for חליצה or יבום
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains 'see children to your children, peace upon ישראל': once there are grandchildren, there is no need for חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And see children to your children, peace upon ישראל.' רבי יהושע בן לוי said: once there are children to your children, there is peace upon ישראל, because they will not come to חליצה and יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another פסוק from תהלים about grandchildren. רבי יהושע בן לוי explains why grandchildren bring peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה and יבום only happen when a man dies with no children. If your children have children, that situation does not come up, and the family is spared it. That is the 'peace' the פסוק talks about.

keyTerms.meaning: Children to your children, meaning grandchildren
The ceremony that frees a childless widow from marrying her husband's brother
When a brother marries the widow of his brother who died without children
Because he will not come to

phrases.english: 'And see children to your children,
peace upon Israel.'
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Once there are 'children to your children' —
there is 'peace upon Israel.'
Since they will not come to chalitzah and yibum.
phrases.notes: These only come up when a man dies without children, so grandchildren mean the family avoids them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְאֵה בָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ שָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק, still on the theme of children and family.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grandchildren bring peace because the family will not need חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: Grandchildren bring peace to the judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads the same פסוק differently: grandchildren bring peace to the judges of ישראל, since people will not come to fight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: once there are children to your children, there is peace upon the judges of ישראל, because people will not come to fight.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא explains the same פסוק in a different way. For him, the peace is for the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי said the peace is for the family. רבי שמואל בר נחמני adds the word 'judges': when there are clear children and grandchildren, people do not end up fighting in front of the court. Same פסוק, different kind of peace.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
Once there are 'children to your children' —
there is peace upon the judges of Israel,
since they will not come to quarrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁבָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grandchildren bring peace to the judges, because people will not come to fight in court.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the teaching of רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its opening words about the דרשה רבי אלעזר taught before the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This דרשה was taught by רבי אלעזר before the חכמים,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion is over, and the גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה. This line sets up the next discussion about that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא only quotes the first few words of the משנה and writes 'וכו׳' to point to the rest. This tells the learner that a new section is starting, based on the next part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned out from the words of a פסוק
And so on; the rest of the quote

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. It is the גמרא quoting the משנה again so it can start discussing it.

phrases.english: This teaching Rabbi Elazar taught
before the Sages, and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה מִדְרָשׁ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the side discussion about פסוקים and goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about the דרשה רבי אלעזר taught before the חכמים.
